## Data cleaning
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)

clean_air <- function(file_path, o3_unit = "ppm") {

  o3_unit <- match.arg(o3_unit, c("ppm", "ppb"))

  data <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%

    # Remove exact duplicate rows
    distinct() %>%

    # Rename variables and convert dates
    transmute(
      date = mdy(Date),
      co = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
      pm25 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
      o3 = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`
    ) %>%

    # Replace negative concentrations with zero
    mutate(across(c(co, pm25, o3),
                  ~ if_else(!is.na(.x) & .x < 0,
                            0, .x))) %>%

    # Calculate one average per day
    group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(
      across(
        c(co, pm25, o3),
        ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        ),
      .groups = "drop"
      )

  # Convert ozone to ppb when requested
  if (o3_unit == "ppb") {
    data <- data %>% mutate(o3 = o3 * 1000)
  }

  return(data)
}
```
The air quality datasets were cleaned by removing duplicate records, converting dates, replacing negative pollutant concentrations with zero, and calculating daily averages for repeated measurements.

## Process and combine all three datasets
```{r}
aq2018 <- clean_air("721_Project2_Data/AQ_2018.csv")
aq2019 <- clean_air("721_Project2_Data/AQ_2019.csv")
aq2020 <- clean_air("721_Project2_Data/AQ_2020.csv")

aq_all <- bind_rows(aq2018, aq2019, aq2020) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date)
  )
```
```{r, include=FALSE}
# Check the cleaned dataset
glimpse(aq_all)
```
The cleaned datasets from 2018, 2019, and 2020 were combined into a single dataset containing 847 daily observations for subsequent analysis.

## Tables
```{r}
make_table <- function(data, selected_year) {

  data %>%
    filter(year == selected_year) %>%
    summarise(
      across(c(co, pm25, o3),
             list(
               Min = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
               Max = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
             ))
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      everything(),
      names_to = c("Pollutant", ".value"),
      names_sep = "_"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Pollutant = recode(
        Pollutant,
        co = "CO (ppm)",
        pm25 = "PM2.5 (ug/m3)",
        o3 = "O3 (ppm)"
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      across(c(Min, Max), ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x))
      ) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      digits = 3,
      caption = paste(
        "Minimum and Maximum Daily Concentrations,",
        selected_year
      )
    )
}

make_table(aq_all, 2018)
make_table(aq_all, 2019)
make_table(aq_all, 2020)
```


## Plot 1: CO and O3 by month.
```{r}
# Calculating monthly means and CI

plot1_data <- aq_all %>%
  select(month, co, o3) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co, o3),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) %>%
  group_by(month, pollutant) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(concentration)),
    mean = mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    lower = mean - 1.96 * sd / sqrt(n),
    upper = mean + 1.96 * sd / sqrt(n),
    pollutant = recode(
      pollutant,
      co = "CO (ppm)",
      o3 = "O3 (ppm)"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# Creating the Plot

ggplot(plot1_data,
       aes(x = month, y = mean,
           color = pollutant)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ pollutant, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb,
    guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)
    ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CO (ppm)" = "#D77A9D",
      "O3 (ppm)" = "#3977A8"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly CO and O3 Concentrations",
    subtitle = "Pooled daily observations, 2018–2020",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Monthly Mean Concentration",
    color = "Pollutant"
  ) +
    theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 60,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 8
    ),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

CO and O3 are displayed in separate panels with independent y-axis scales because their concentrations differ substantially. This allows the monthly patterns and confidence intervals for both pollutants to be clearly visible.

## Plot 2: PM2.5 by month and year
```{r}
# Calculating the monthly PM2.5 averages separately for each year

plot2_data <- aq_all %>%
  group_by(year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# Create the plot

ggplot(plot2_data,
       aes(x = month,
           y = mean_pm25,
           color = factor(year),
           group = year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "2018" = "#D77A9D",
      "2019" = "#3977A8",
      "2020" = "#55A68C"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean PM2.5 (ug/m3)",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

I used a line plot with points because it clearly displays monthly trends and makes it easy to compare PM2.5 concentrations across the three years.


## Interpretation

CO concentrations tended to be higher during late fall and winter, while O3 concentrations were generally higher in spring and summer. PM2.5 concentrations varied across years, with relatively high values in summer and December 2018 and early 2019. Since the 2020 dataset only includes January through April, comparisons for the remaining months are limited to 2018 and 2019.
